principles.statement: Transport connectivity does not imply data freshness, equipment health, operability, command eligibility, or control authority.
Products calculate domain truth; LDS presents named state, evidence, time, reason, and recovery affordance without running the product state machine.
Unknown is a first-class observation state and must not be normalized to positive, negative, disconnected, or unavailable.
A retained last-known value must expose freshness or observation time and must not be presented as current truth.
Semantic state, visual tone, and announcement urgency are separate decisions.
Stable states and transition states remain distinguishable; transition execution and recovery policy stay product-owned.

transport.definition: Whether the application has a transport link and the quality of that link.
transport.productOwns: Protocol truth, retry, heartbeat, reconnect, resynchronization, and timeout policy.
transport.ldsOwns: Named transport presentation, non-color marker, reduced-motion behavior, and accessible name.

freshness.definition: Whether the displayed observation is current enough for its product-defined decision window.
freshness.productOwns: Clock source, freshness threshold, observation age, cache policy, and resynchronization completion.
freshness.ldsOwns: Freshness label, observation time placement, retained-value treatment, and non-color stale cue.

health.definition: A product-provided diagnostic assessment of the observed entity.
health.productOwns: Diagnosis, thresholds, aggregation, causal evidence, and recovery policy.
health.ldsOwns: Visible health name, semantic tone, supporting evidence placement, and color-independent cue.

operability.definition: Whether the user may currently use the entity for the intended product action.
operability.productOwns: Admission policy, blockers, permissions, safety gates, and reason ordering.
operability.ldsOwns: Availability name, blocker presentation, disabled-reason association, and recovery affordance placement.

authority.definition: Whether the current actor holds the product-defined right to control or approve the target.
authority.productOwns: Authorization, lease, takeover, expiry, revocation, and conflict policy.
authority.ldsOwns: Authority state presentation, blocking reason, transition message, and re-acquisition affordance placement.

command.definition: The product-reported lifecycle of a requested external or domain change.
command.productOwns: Eligibility, payload, authorization, idempotency, transport, execution, watcher, and result truth.
command.ldsOwns: Distinct lifecycle labels, progress/result hierarchy, retry affordance placement, and announcement urgency.

evidence.definition: Whether source material or observed evidence is available and usable for the current claim.
evidence.productOwns: Source truth, access, retrieval, interpretation, sufficiency, and citation policy.
evidence.ldsOwns: Availability label, source identity, observation/update time, excerpt hierarchy, and return action.

review.definition: Whether a human decision is required and the product-reported result of that decision.
review.productOwns: Reviewer eligibility, policy, assignment, persistence, override, and final decision truth.
review.ldsOwns: Review state label, evidence grouping, decision control composition, and result presentation.

urgency.definition: How urgently a state transition requires user attention; urgency is not the entity state or visual tone.
urgency.productOwns: Escalation, acknowledgement, suppression, notification channel, and incident policy.
urgency.ldsOwns: Status versus alert announcement behavior, visible urgency label, and non-color emphasis.

research.title: ROS 2 Managed nodes
research.conclusion: Keep stable states distinct from transitions and leave transition execution to a supervisory product layer.

research.title: Open-RMF RobotState
research.conclusion: Mode, battery, location, path, task identity, and message sequence are independent evidence; connection alone cannot establish freshness or health.

research.title: Kubernetes Pod Conditions
research.conclusion: Unknown, transition time, machine reason, and human message are explicit condition evidence, and composite readiness depends on multiple conditions.

research.title: W3C WCAG Technique ARIA19
research.conclusion: Assertive alerts are disruptive and should be reserved for changes that require immediate attention rather than routine status presentation.
